clean_story:
"Global connections. Instant sharing.

The name internet comes from 'interconnected networks,' as it links computers worldwide to exchange data.

Most think the internet appeared overnight, yet it grew from a 1960s military experiment called ARPANET, designed to keep communication alive even if parts were destroyed. Like a spiderweb where cutting one thread leaves the rest intact. The first message sent in 1969—'LOGIN'—crashed after two letters, revealing its fragility and promise. By 1983, TCP/IP became the universal language, letting different networks merge into one. Today, packets of data race across cables and satellites, reassembling in milliseconds like a puzzle solving itself. Without this, no emails, no videos, no maps guiding you home.

Three related subjects are packet switching, network protocols and digital communication."
